source.how: Each sheet's Local_Street map frame carries a GeoPDF /VP viewport with its corner coordinates (NAD83 HARN geographic, projected to EPSG:2913); a page-to-ground affine was fitted to them. Bull Mountain's sheet is a raster and Raleigh Hills' carries the same fill as vector paths, so both were read one way: the page rendered at 432 dpi (4.63 ft a pixel), the 'Local Street Connectivity Lands' green (R 40-140, G > 200, B < 80) masked inside the main frame (legend and inset excluded), the mask closed by 3 pixels to fill the taxlot lines the map draws over it, and each pixel placed by the frame's affine. A residential lot's share is the masked ground over its area 6 ft in from its lines (so a pixel lost at the lot line is not read as the map's edge): at least 90 percent is inside, held whole; more than 10 percent and less is cut, carried as its masked part (pixel gaps closed by 3 ft and simplified at 3 ft) at its share, so the screen leaves it unanswered; a cut lot whose part falls within 12 percent of either band edge is carried whole instead, so it is held and never read as outside. Inside means the plan's on-site street standards reach the lot's development (Bull Mountain: block lengths of 530 ft, perimeters of 1,800 ft, no cul-de-sacs, connection to stub streets; Raleigh Hills: Local Streets required to connect, or accessways where impracticable), and an on-site street takes ground nothing measures. The chunk 6 plans (Aloha - Reedville - Cooper Mountain, Cedar Hills - Cedar Mill, Sunset West, Bethany Chapter 1; 2026-10-31) were read the same way from the same county map template: each Local_Street frame's own /VP viewport, the same green, the same 432 dpi render, closing, 6 ft core and bands, and zones R-5 to R-25+ (a non-residential lot is not carried). Sheets that overlap (Aloha's three, Cedar Hills' and Sunset West's two each) were OR'd on a 5 ft ground grid. Their text is Raleigh Hills' word for word: the map 'indicates where, as part of development, 1) Local Streets are required to connect to the existing system'. Many of the lands shown green have been divided and built since the sheets were printed; they are held all the same, as the coordinator ruling holds Raleigh Hills'.
